answer: Ephemeral Lottery Partitioning. Agents wander into random shards drawn from a beacon the attacker cannot predict before commit. Each identity must submit a unique proof bound to its shard assignment; only one per shard threshold is admitted, and duplicates are dropped. An attacker cannot precompute placements, so forcing N live identities costs N separate unpredictable draws, wasted registrations, and repeated beacon-bound work—linear waste per sybil, plus failed placements. Ivory tokens mark admitted shards; an unrelated sparrow signal flags rejected duplicates.
